title: The Book of Revelation: Justice and Judgment
author: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza
summary: Collected essays on the theology, composition and social setting of Revelation, including a proposed seven-part concentric structure of the book centred on the small prophetic scroll (10:1–15:4).

title: Interpreting the Book of Revelation: Hermeneutical Guidelines, with Brief Introduction to Literary Analysis
author: Kenneth A. Strand
summary: Short study that argues Revelation is built as a chiasm of paired sections in inverse order, divided into a historical half (to the end of chapter 14) and an eschatological-judgment half (from chapter 15).

title: Literary Structure—a Key to Interpreting the Revelation (Ministry, March 1977)
author: Kenneth A. Strand
summary: Popular summary of Strand's chiastic outline: prologue and epilogue, church militant and triumphant, God's saving work in progress and completed, and the forces opposing God's people warned and then punished, with the dividing line at the end of chapter 14.

title: The Eight Basic Visions in the Book of Revelation (Andrews University Seminary Studies 25.1, pp. 107-121)
author: Kenneth A. Strand
summary: Refines Strand's outline into eight major visions, four in a historical series and four in an eschatological series, paired in inverse order between a matching prologue and epilogue.

title: The Coherence of the Flood Narrative (Vetus Testamentum 28, pp. 336-348)
author: Gordon J. Wenham
summary: Argues that Genesis 6–9 forms an extended palistrophe (mirror structure) whose turning point is 8:1, 'God remembered Noah'.

title: The Literary Structure of the Old Testament: A Commentary on Genesis–Malachi
author: David A. Dorsey
summary: Book-by-book survey of literary structure in the Old Testament, giving particular attention to symmetrical and chiastic arrangements and their use for emphasis.

title: Daniel: An Introduction and Commentary (Tyndale Old Testament Commentaries)
author: Joyce G. Baldwin
summary: Evangelical commentary that discusses the unity of Daniel and presents, following Lenglet, the concentric arrangement of the Aramaic chapters 2–7.

title: La structure littéraire de Daniel 2–7 (Biblica 53, pp. 169-190)
author: Adolphe Lenglet
summary: Influential article arguing that the Aramaic chapters of Daniel form a concentric unit: chapters 2 and 7 (four kingdoms), 3 and 6 (deliverance of the faithful), and 4 and 5 (judgment on proud kings).

title: Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi: An Introduction and Commentary (Tyndale Old Testament Commentaries)
author: Joyce G. Baldwin
summary: Commentary noting the symmetrical arrangement of Zechariah's night visions, with the outer visions concerning the whole earth and the central ones concerning the leaders of the restored community.

title: Isaiah (NIV Application Commentary)
author: John N. Oswalt
summary: Commentary that sets out Isaiah 56–66 as a concentric structure (56:1–8 / 56:9–59:15a / 59:15b–21 / 60–62 / 63:1–6 / 63:7–66:17 / 66:18–24) with the vision of glorified Zion at its apex.

title: The Chiastic Structure of Amos V 1-17 (Vetus Testamentum 27, pp. 170-177)
author: Jan de Waard
summary: Argues that Amos 5:1–17 is a concentric unit whose centre is the hymn fragment of 5:8–9 proclaiming 'the LORD is his name'.

title: The Structure of Joel (Journal of the Evangelical Theological Society 28.3, pp. 289-297)
author: Duane A. Garrett
summary: Argues that Joel is a single literary and theological unit whose two halves, turning at 2:18, answer each other: devastation answered by restoration and invasion answered by judgment on the nations.

title: The Combat Myth in the Book of Revelation
author: Adela Yarbro Collins
summary: Study of Revelation 12 against ancient combat myths, which also proposes that the book unfolds in two great cycles of visions, the second beginning with the woman, child and dragon in chapter 12.

title: L'utilisation du livre d'Ezéchiel dans l'Apocalypse (Biblica 43, pp. 436-476)
author: Albert Vanhoye
summary: Classic study of Revelation's use of Ezekiel, showing that John draws on Ezekiel more than on almost any other book and broadly follows the order of Ezekiel's visions.
